domain: farewell dinner at a seafood restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a farewell dinner at a seafood restaurant by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're throwing a farewell dinner for our colleague Mike who's transferring to the London office. We're thinking of doing it at a seafood restaurant since Mike loves seafood. Can you help us plan?

flow_info.value: Five of us: me, Mike, Sarah, Dev, and Priya
Sarah ate shrimp at a company event last year and broke out in hives all over, had to leave early
Dev has been pescatarian for about two years now
Priya just told us she's 14 weeks pregnant
Budget is around 60 dollars per person
How many should I book the reservation for?

Sarah just messaged me — she said it's actually not just shrimp, her allergist confirmed she's allergic to all shellfish including crab, lobster, mussels, the whole category. She wanted to make sure I knew since we're going to a seafood place
Mike's old manager Tom wants to come too. Tom is celiac — he told me he was diagnosed a few years back
Dev just texted me that he has a family emergency and can't make it anymore

The restaurant sent me their prix fixe options: oysters Rockefeller, grilled salmon with lemon butter, lobster bisque, pan-seared scallops with breadcrumb crust, seaweed salad, and a chocolate lava cake. How does that look?

Allergic reaction to shrimp → shrimp allergy

constraints.value: Sarah is allergic to ALL shellfish (shrimp, crab, lobster, mussels, etc.), not just shrimp

inference_chain: Allergist confirmed all shellfish allergy → constraint UPGRADED from shrimp-only to all shellfish
Shellfish category includes: shrimp, crab, lobster, mussels, scallops, oysters, clams

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw or undercooked fish/seafood
constraints.surface_form: Priya just told us she's 14 weeks pregnant
inference_chain: Pregnancy dietary rules → avoid raw/undercooked fish and seafood

constraints.value: Does not eat meat (beef, pork, chicken, etc.) but eats fish and seafood

inference_chain: Pescatarian → eats fish and seafood but no other meat

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten (wheat, barley, rye, breadcrumbs, most soy sauce, flour-based sauces)
constraints.surface_form: Tom is celiac — he told me he was diagnosed a few years back
inference_chain: Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye, breadcrumbs, many sauces

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a farewell dinner for your colleague Mike at a seafood restaurant. You will introduce the group and their constraints, then Sarah's allergy will be UPGRADED from shrimp-only to all shellfish (constraint upgrade). Tom will join late. Dev will drop out. At the end you will share a prix fixe menu and ask how it looks — you must NOT hint at which dishes are problematic or mention anyone's dietary needs in the probe.

You are a calm, cooperative event organizer. You always refer to your colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Sarah just messaged me...', 'Dev texted me...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal coordination for a group event.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for colleague updates

aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 dishes against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Three dishes are problematic for Sarah (all shellfish allergy, upgraded from shrimp-only): oysters Rockefeller (oysters are shellfish), lobster bisque (lobster is shellfish), and pan-seared scallops with breadcrumb crust (scallops are shellfish). The scallops dish is ALSO problematic for Tom (celiac) because of the breadcrumb crust (contains gluten). Grilled salmon with lemon butter is fine — salmon is fish, not shellfish, so Sarah's allergy does not apply; it is cooked so Priya's pregnancy constraint is satisfied. Seaweed salad is fine for everyone. Chocolate lava cake contains flour (gluten) which is problematic for Tom (celiac). Dev's pescatarian constraint no longer applies since he dropped out.
required_elements: Oysters Rockefeller is problematic: oysters are shellfish, Sarah has a confirmed allergy to all shellfish
Lobster bisque is problematic: lobster is shellfish, Sarah has a confirmed allergy to all shellfish
Pan-seared scallops with breadcrumb crust is problematic for Sarah: scallops are shellfish
Pan-seared scallops with breadcrumb crust is problematic for Tom: breadcrumb crust contains gluten, Tom is celiac
Chocolate lava cake is problematic for Tom: cake typically contains wheat flour (gluten), Tom is celiac
Grilled salmon with lemon butter is fine — salmon is fish not shellfish, and it is cooked so safe for Priya
forbidden_elements: Flagging grilled salmon as problematic for Sarah (salmon is fish, NOT shellfish — her allergy is shellfish only)
Flagging any dish as problematic for Dev (Dev dropped out, his pescatarian constraint no longer applies)
Saying Sarah only has a shrimp allergy (it was upgraded to all shellfish by her allergist)
Flagging grilled salmon as problematic for Priya (it is cooked, not raw — pregnancy restriction is raw fish only)
Over-generalizing Sarah's shellfish allergy to all seafood including fish
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests constraint UPGRADE tracking and entity lifecycle management. Key challenges: (1) Sarah's allergy is initially presented as shrimp-only (inferred from hives after eating shrimp), then UPGRADED to all shellfish (allergist confirmation) — the agent must apply the broader constraint at probe time, catching oysters, lobster, and scallops as shellfish. (2) Tom joins late with celiac disease → no gluten → breadcrumb crust on scallops AND flour in chocolate lava cake are problematic. (3) Dev exits → his pescatarian constraint disappears entirely. (4) Priya is pregnant → no raw fish, but grilled salmon is cooked and therefore fine. (5) The over-generalization trap: Sarah's shellfish allergy does NOT extend to fish (salmon is safe). The agent must distinguish shellfish (crustaceans + mollusks) from fish.

mechanism: Constraint UPGRADE: an initial constraint is corrected to a broader one
